name: Da Nang Cathedral
kicker: The pink church called the rooster church
summary: Look up at the pink church the city calls Con Ga, the rooster church, a short walk from the river. It was built in 1923, nearly 70 meters, in a Gothic form, under Father Louis Vallet. The parish page prints no street number, no Mass clock, and no fee. All three stay check on arrival.
getThere: In the center. The parish page does not print a street number. Ask for Nhà thờ Con Gà.
heroCaption: The pink facade and the rose window

notice.title: The rooster is not a French emblem
notice.body: An English tourism page calls the bird a French symbol. The Vietnamese parish page says the priest explains it as Peter in the Gospel, a call to wake up, not as France. The official parish name dates from 1963.

body: Give it the few minutes a church front takes, on a river morning. The city parish page says the church was built in 1923, nearly 70 meters high, under Father Louis Vallet, in a Gothic form with a rose window. Behind it is a grotto of Our Lady arranged after Lourdes. People in the city call it Con Gà, the rooster church, for the bird on the roof.

That page says the bird is Peter, not a symbol of France, and that from 1963 the parish’s official name is Nhà thờ giáo xứ Chánh tòa Đà Nẵng. It does not print a street number, a Mass time, or a fee. Do not copy a tour company’s visiting window onto this page. Hours, a closing day, and any fee are check on arrival.

gettingThere: The parish page does not print a street number. From a river hotel, ask for Nhà thờ Con Gà. From My Khe, take a Grab. Neither ride has a published minute count, so both stay check on arrival.
